None of these cause any execution during sourcing: the `source` line is a passive string definition that does not trigger a network download until `makepkg` proceeds to the download step, and checksums are never verified during `--printsrcinfo`. There is no `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, `base64`, command substitution, or any other construct that could download or execute untrusted code while the file is parsed.

The `build()` and `package()` functions (only running `make` and `make install DESTDIR="$pkgdir"`) are out of scope for this gate and would be audited in the full PKGBUILD review, but they appear to be routine upstream build/install practices.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>

</summary>
